name: Compute Express Link 2.0
bandwidth_basis: x16, PER DIRECTION, full duplex. CXL 2.0 runs on the PCIe 5.0 physical layer (32 GT/s with 128b/130b coding): 3.938 GB/s per lane per direction, 63.015 GB/s BIDIRECTIONAL AGGREGATE at x16, so the recorded per-direction value is 31.5 GB/s. The consortium's own 4.0 page confirms 2.0 is the 32 GT/s base of the family and that 4.0 'doubles the bandwidth from 64GTs to 128GTs'.
topology: Point-to-point device attachment over PCIe PHY, extended with switching and memory pooling so a single host can reach pooled memory devices across a CXL domain.
switching: CXL 2.0 is where switching and memory pooling enter the family: multiple hosts can share a switched pool of memory devices, coherently, unlike DDR.
notes: Inference consequence: CXL is a memory-capacity and coherency tier, not a tensor-parallel tier. At 31.5 GB/s per direction it is roughly 7x below PCIe 5.0 host attach per lane set on any realistic comparison of use, and 14x below NVLink 4, so KV-cache spilling to CXL memory saves HBM capacity but costs latency on every attention read. CXL 2.0 is sufficient for that only when the spill is streaming-batched; per-token sequential KV reads over CXL latency will show up directly in inter-token latency. The consortium page confirms full backward compatibility down to CXL 1.0/1.1.
